script: A delivery truck has reached the main gate. Where should the driver wait before entering?
Where should the driver park first?
Park in the waiting area, switch off the engine, and walk to Security.
Wait in the waiting area with the engine off. Do not drive straight inside.
The driver has five documents. Match each one to the right desk.
Sort each incoming document to the correct reception desk.
Security checks driver and vehicle documents. The Data Entry Operator checks shipping papers and prepares the gate pass.
Send Purchase Order, Advanced Shipping Notice, and invoice to the Data Entry Operator. Send the driver's license and vehicle papers to Security.
The Data Entry Operator enters the invoice in the system. The system checks whether the truck delivery matches the Advanced Shipping Notice.
What does this system check do if the Advanced Shipping Notice is wrong?
The system fills the shipment details from the Advanced Shipping Notice. If it does not match, stop the gate entry until it is corrected.
Do not bypass a mismatch. If the Advanced Shipping Notice is wrong, stop the gate entry and get it corrected.

The Data Entry Operator runs the gate entry pass! The printer outputs the windshield barcode pass while the driver watches the status TV. Can you place the driver's gate journey in exact chronological order?
Arrange the driver's gate entry journey in the correct chronological order.

Flawless sequence! Following the exact order from parking to credentials check, ERP validation, barcode pass issuance, and finally dock entry prevents gate congestion and ensures 100 percent material traceability.
Hold on! The driver cannot move to the dock before collecting the printed barcode pass. Let's arrange the steps in the correct order.
The Data Entry Operator assigns the warehouse dock! Based on our shipment of vehicle mechanical parts, which warehouse dock on the Auric plant layout must be allocated?
The Data Entry Operator assigns the warehouse dock for vehicle assembly parts. Tap the correct allocated bay & dock on the Auric plant layout.
Spot on! Dock 04 in Inbound Bay B is designated for vehicle assembly components. Dock 01 is reserved for battery cells and Dock 06 for hazardous chemicals.
Careful! Dock 01 is an environmentally controlled vault for battery cells only, and Dock 06 is for chemicals. Vehicle parts belong at Dock 04.
The truck is docked at Bay B, Dock 04! Before keys and invoices are handed over and unloading begins, inspect the vehicle for a critical safety violation.
Spot the immediate safety violation before keys are accepted and unloading starts.
Lifesaving catch! Heavy rubber wheel chocks be placed under rear tires to prevent trailer roll-away when forklifts enter.
High danger alert! If a 3-ton forklift drives inside an unchocked trailer, trailer creep will cause the forklift to plunge into the dock gap!

Unloading is done! The truck has loaded 20 empty blue Foldable Large Container bins to return to the vendor. At the exit gate, the driver demands: 'Open the boom barrier, these are just Ather's empty bins!' What must you do?
The driver wants to leave with 20 empty Foldable Large Container bins without a manual Delivery Challan.
Brilliant vigilance! Returnable bins/Foldable Large Containers require an authorized manual Delivery Challan and system exit clearance before the exit gate barrier opens!

Stop! Never raise the barrier without a manual Delivery Challan. Empty Foldable Large Container bins are valuable Ather company assets. Without a Delivery Challan, thousands of rupees of packaging exit untracked!

Attention Data Entry Operator! The driver presents an invoice for 50 battery harnesses, but the digital Advanced Shipping Notice in SAP lists 40 pieces for this Purchase Order. Can gate entry proceed?
The physical invoice quantity differs from the digital Advanced Shipping Notice in SAP.

Correct decision! Never generate a gate pass for a mismatched Advanced Shipping Notice. The Data Entry Operator halts the transaction and alerts the Inbound Gate Incharge within 1 hour to resolve the vendor Advanced Shipping Notice discrepancy.
Violation! Generating a gate pass with an incorrect Advanced Shipping Notice creates major inventory mismatches in SAP ERP that block quality inspection receiving and vendor payment clearance.

A scheduled chassis frame truck reports at Gate 01. However, the SAP inventory screen indicates that High-Rise Rack storage for frames is already at 100 percent maximum capacity! What is the mandatory Data Entry Operator action?
The maximum stock capacity for this material is full in the warehouse. What must the Data Entry Operator do?

Spot-on! The truck remains in the designated waiting parking area until line assembly consumes existing stock and clears warehouse pallet positions. Dumping material on dock gangways is strictly forbidden.
Incorrect! Never dump material in active dock corridors or send the supplier away. Truck must wait in parking bay until pallet locations clear.

Welcome to Stage 2: Receiving & quality inspection Clearance! The forklift has offloaded a pallet of brake calipers at Dock 04 Inbound Staging. Look closely at the freshly pasted Goods Receipt Note sticker on the pallet. What does that large '?' symbol tell us?
Forklifts have offloaded the pallet into Inbound Staging. You inspect the freshly pasted Goods Receipt Note sticker and spot a large '?' printed on it. What does this symbol mean?

Spot on! A '?' on the Goods Receipt Note sticker designates Non-Direct-on-Line material. It requires mandatory 10 percent sampling and testing by quality inspection before it can be put away into storage!

Hold on! A '?' symbol does not mean scrap or direct-to-line. It means Non-Direct-on-Line—the material must undergo mandatory quality inspection sampling. Premature put-away of uninspected stock will be blocked by SAP warehouse management system!

Now that we know the shipment is Non-Direct-on-Line, we must apply the 10 percent statistical sampling rule! The Purchase Order contains 10 Foldable Large Container crates (100 total brake calipers). Exactly how many Foldable Large Container crates must be separated and transferred to the quality inspection testing area?

A Non-Direct-on-Line lot of 10 Foldable Large Containers has arrived. following the standard 10 percent statistical sampling rule, how many Foldable Large Container crates must go to quality inspection?

Spot on! Exactly 10 percent of the lot volume (1 out of 10 Foldable Large Containers) is transferred to quality inspection staging. The remaining 9 Foldable Large Containers must stay safely in unloading staging until quality inspection clears the sample!

Calculation error! Exactly 10 percent of the inward volume must be sampled. For a 10-Foldable Large Container lot, sending more than 1 Foldable Large Container clutters the test lab, while sending less violates ISO/standard operating procedure statistical standards.

The 1 sample crate has gone to the testing lab, but 9 crates of brake calipers are waiting in Inbound Staging! While quality inspection inspects the sample for up to 2 hours, what mandatory visual identifier must be placed around this staged lot?
The 9 remaining Foldable Large Container crates are waiting in staging during the 2-hour quality inspection testing window. What mandatory visual containment must be placed around them?

Spot on! Bright yellow 'UNDER quality inspection' cones must be placed at the staging perimeter. This visual quarantine stops forklift drivers from mistakenly picking or putting away uninspected stock!

Quality risk! Never leave uninspected staging unmarked. Yellow 'UNDER quality inspection' cones are mandatory. Red tags are only for confirmed scrap, and green seals require a passed inspection report.

The Goods Receipt Note sticker is pasted and the 10 percent sample is loaded onto the pallet truck! The factory clock is ticking. What is the maximum permissible SLA time window for inbound manpower to physically hand over this sample to the quality inspection testing room?
Following Goods Receipt Note label application, what is the strict SLA cutoff time for inbound manpower to hand over Non-Direct-on-Line samples to the quality inspection testing room?

Precision timing! Inbound manpower must hand over the Non-Direct-on-Line sample to quality inspection within exactly 30 minutes of Goods Receipt Note pasting. Meeting this SLA ensures the 2-hour testing window finishes before production needs the parts!

SLA breach warning! Delaying sample handover beyond 30 minutes leaves the Warehouse Order open in SAP warehouse management system. This blocks subsequent picking orders and delays vehicle assembly line feeding!

The quality inspection inspector has finished testing the sample! The incoming lot will receive one of 3 distinct outcomes: Pass, Hold, or NG (Rejected). Warehouse operators must execute the exact physical standard operating procedure disposition protocol for each result. Match each action item to its correct outcome bucket!
Match the Incoming Quality Control (quality inspection) outcome to the mandatory physical warehouse action.

Flawless quality compliance! For PASS, seal the green 'QC Pass' on the Goods Receipt Note sticker to release put-away. For HOLD, place the yellow 'quality inspection Hold' cone. For NG, attach the red NG tag, log a Jira bug ticket with Part # and Lot ID, and transfer the entire lot volume to quarantine area Quarantine Storage by designated NG manpower! Module 2 Receiving & quality inspection Clearance is now 100 percent complete!

Disposition protocol error! Never move unsealed parts to High-Rise Racks. When a lot fails, the ENTIRE lot volume must be quarantined with an active Jira defect ticket, not just the defective sample pieces!

Welcome to the quality inspection quality gate! Every pallet offloaded at Dock 04 undergoes strict verification. What does quality inspection stand for, and what is its primary operational role in Ather Auric Plant M002?
What does quality inspection stand for, and what is its primary purpose at Ather Auric?
Correct! quality inspection stands for Incoming Quality Control. Their team tests incoming supplier components against technical blueprints before parts enter production storage.
Incorrect. quality inspection stands for Incoming Quality Control, ensuring zero defect parts reach vehicle assembly lines.
Under Ather Quality Policy, during the first 6 months of a new factory launch (Auric Plant ramp-up), which inward supplier materials must be routed to quality inspection before put-away?
In a new factory, during the first 6 months, which inward parts must go to quality inspection?

Exactly right! During the initial 6-month ramp-up phase, Direct-on-Line (Direct-on-Line) privileges are suspended. 100 percent of all inward parts are treated as Non-Direct-on-Line to validate supplier consistency.
Careful! For the first 6 months of plant launch, ALL incoming supplier parts must undergo quality inspection inspection to establish baseline quality.
Mastering the chronological rhythm of receiving is essential! Arrange the 4 mandatory operational stages of Non-Direct-on-Line material receiving in the correct order.
Put the Non-Direct-on-Line Receiving and quality inspection steps in correct chronological order.

Outstanding! Unload & paste Goods Receipt Note label then Collect 10 percent sample & place Under quality inspection cones then Physical handover to lab within 30-min SLA then Issue Pass, Hold, or NG disposition.
Out of sequence! The Goods Receipt Note label must be pasted before sampling, and the 10 percent sample must be demarcated with cones before lab handover.

Non-Direct-on-Line sample crates have been sitting in receiving staging for 75 minutes because the team was busy offloading another truck! What is the critical systemic risk of exceeding the 30-minute handover SLA?
Non-Direct-on-Line samples are not issued to quality inspection within the 30-minute SLA. What is the operational risk?
Spot-on! If samples are not issued within 30 minutes, the open SAP WH order stays locked, blocking put-away tasks for all subsequent shipments and starving the vehicle assembly line.
Violation! Delayed quality inspection handover deadlocks the SAP warehouse management system queue. Inbound Zone Leader must immediately prioritize sample delivery to clear the system block.

Welcome to Stage 3: Vehicle & Battery Parts Put-Away! The incoming brake caliper lot has passed inspection and carries the green 'QC Pass' seal. An Material Handling Equipment reach-truck operator arrives with a rugged handheld terminal. Before moving any pallet toward the racks, what mandatory digital scan must be performed to initiate the SAP warehouse management system Warehouse Task?
In Goods Receipt Note staging, what must the Material Handling Equipment operator scan first with the rugged handheld terminal to generate the Put-Away Warehouse Task?

Standard procedure verified! The operator must scan the pallet-level Handling Unit barcode on the Goods Receipt Note sticker first. Scanning the Handling Unit instructs SAP warehouse management system to generate the Warehouse Task, displaying the target High-Rise Rack bin and part specifications!

Incorrect scan sequence! You cannot begin put-away without scanning the Handling Unit label first. Moving material before the Handling Unit scan leaves SAP warehouse management system blind to pallet movement, causing open task backlogs and ERP stock mismatch.

The Handling Unit has been scanned and the warehouse task is active! The forklift reaches a major internal warehouse junction with two diverging paths. Inbound materials arrive in two different packaging forms: standard blue Foldable Large Container crates and specialized wheeled body trolleys. How must these two material streams be segregated?
Where must each incoming container type be routed at the warehouse junction?

Spot on! Standard Foldable Large Container crates and bins are routed to High-Rise Racks for vertical stowing via reach-trucks, while large body frames and battery modules on heavy trolleys are moved directly to the designated Trolley Staging Area for direct line feeding!

Route routing error! Wheeled trolleys cannot be placed on High-Rise Racks due to beam clearance and weight distribution hazards, and Foldable Large Container pallets cannot block the floor-level trolley feeding lanes!

The reach-truck has safely transported the Foldable Large Container pallet down Aisle B of the High-Rise Racks. The hydraulic forks elevate the pallet onto shelf level 4 at bin location Rack Bin B-04. The pallet is physically resting on the steel beam. What final mandatory action must the operator execute right now before driving away?
The Foldable Large Container pallet is resting on shelf Rack Beam B-04. What mandatory action must the operator execute to formally conclude the put-away?

Masterful execution! The operator must scan the location QR code on rack beam Rack Bin B-04. This marries the pallet Handling Unit to the specific storage bin in SAP warehouse management system, updates system G-stock, and closes the active Warehouse Task!

Critical omission! Leaving the rack without scanning the location QR code leaves the Warehouse Task open in SAP warehouse management system. The inventory remains invisible to picking teams and negatively impacts your operator efficiency KPI!

Alert! A trainee operator lifted a pallet of 100 brake calipers onto Rack Beam B-04, lowered the forks, and immediately drove away toward the breakroom without scanning the rack QR code. What is the immediate operational and systemic impact of omitting this scan?
An Material Handling Equipment operator placed an Foldable Large Container pallet into the rack but forgot to scan the destination location QR code before driving away. What happens?

Critical standard operating procedure insight! Because the destination scan was skipped, SAP warehouse management system leaves the Warehouse Task in an 'OPEN' state. The stock is never posted to active G-stock, making it invisible to downstream assembly line pickers, and the overdue task reflects directly as a negative breach on the operator's efficiency KPI! The Zone Leader must intervene to manually trace and close the task.

Misconception! ERP systems cannot detect physical placement without a confirmation barcode scan. Skipping the scan does NOT automatically complete; instead, it creates ghost inventory, keeps the Warehouse Task open, and breaches your individual KPI performance.

Critical situation on Aisle 04! Your handheld terminal screen clearly displays assigned destination bin assigned Bin A-02. However, that bin is high on level 2. The operator notices an empty lower rack lower Bin B-03 nearby and decides to put the pallet into Bin B instead to save time. Should this action be allowed or stopped?
The SAP handheld displays assigned Bin A, but the operator places the pallet into Bin B to save time. What must be done?

STOP IS THE ONLY CORRECT ACTION! The system strictly dictates storage bins based on First-In First-Out, part weight, and pick frequency algorithms. Putting stock in an unassigned bin creates severe inventory discrepancies. The system will NOT close the Warehouse Task unless the assigned bin is scanned. You must either move it to Bin A or request the Zone Leader to re-slot in SAP warehouse management system!

CRITICAL STORAGE MISMATCH! Placing pallets in unassigned bins causes 'ghost stockouts' during assembly line picking. The system will flag an open task against your ID and picking operators will find an empty bin!

Final Put-Away certification milestone! You have mastered the rules of handling units, high-rise racks, bin marriage, and error recovery. Now prove your operational mastery by arranging the complete put-away lifecycle in its exact chronological order!
Arrange the 5 mandatory put-away steps in the exact operational sequence

OUTSTANDING ACCURACY! You have successfully mastered the official sequence: First, Paste Goods Receipt Note label, Second, Scan Handling Unit label, Third, Carry pallet to the location, Fourth, Scan location QR code, Task closes and SAP stock updates! Stage 3: Vehicle & Battery Parts Put-Away is 100 percent complete!

Incorrect sequence! Remember The Goods Receipt Note label must be pasted first, followed by scanning the Handling Unit to initiate the task, transporting to the bin, scanning the rack QR, and finally system closure!

Welcome to Stage 4: Specialized Battery Cell Put-Away! High-value lithium-ion battery cell crates have arrived at Dock 01. These sensitive cells power the Ather 450-X and are hazardous if mishandled. A general warehouse helper grabs a manual pallet truck to move the pallet to clear the dock floor. Should they proceed?
A general warehouse helper attempts to move an unloaded lithium-ion battery cell pallet using a manual Hand Pallet Truck to clear the dock floor. Allow or halt this transfer?

STOP IS CORRECT! Battery cells must be handled and transported EXCLUSIVELY by certified Material Handling Equipment operators using designated electric reach-trucks or powered pallet trucks. Uncertified handling risks thermal shocks, mechanical puncture, or dangerous cell dropping!

CRITICAL SAFETY VIOLATION! General warehouse associates and manual helpers are strictly prohibited from moving lithium-ion cell shipments. Mishandling fragile battery cells can cause internal short circuits, fire hazards, and complete warranty voiding.

The certified Material Handling Equipment operator has transported the lithium-ion cell pallet through the airlock into the sealed Battery Standard Room. Before stowing the pallet into the cell vault, the environmental telemetry monitors must be verified. What are the strict temperature and relative humidity thresholds mandated by standard procedure?
Under Ather Auric what are the mandatory environmental thresholds for the Battery Cell Standard Room?

Exact environmental calibration! The Battery Standard Room must maintain 20 degrees Celsius–25 degrees Celsius temperature and 60 percent–65 percent Relative Humidity (RH) 24/7. This prevents thermal runaway, electrolyte crystallization, and moisture absorption inside cathode/anode layers!

Environmental non-compliance! Exceeding 25 degrees Celsius accelerates internal cell degradation, while dropping below 60 percent or exceeding 65 percent humidity creates condensation and static discharge hazards around sensitive battery terminals.

Pay close attention to the warehouse clock! Lithium-ion battery cell pallets cannot sit idling on the open receiving dock. Uncontrolled ambient temperature and humidity accelerate electrochemical degradation. Under Ather what is the mandatory maximum SLA window within which the entire battery cell put-away must be completed?
Under Ather Auric what is the mandatory maximum SLA window for completing battery cell put-away from Goods Receipt Note staging into the standard room?

SLA compliance verified! Put-away from Goods Receipt Note staging into the Battery Standard Room has a strict 2-hour SLA. This guarantees that sensitive lithium-ion cells are protected inside the 20 degrees Celsius–25 degrees Celsius cleanroom before thermal stress or moisture can impact cell life!

SLA BREACH HAZARD! Leaving battery cells on the open dock beyond 2 hours violates Ather quality protocols. Ambient dock heat and humidity accelerate cell self-discharge and pose severe fire risks. The SLA is strictly 2 hours!

ALARM TRIPPED! As you prepare to complete cell vault put-away, the wall telemetry strobe begins flashing amber: Relative Humidity has spiked to 75.2 percent and temperature is rising to 27.4 degrees Celsius. Moisture is dangerous for exposed battery electrodes! What is your immediate mandatory escalation action under Ather?

While transporting lithium-ion cells into the Standard Room, the wall telemetry flashes an amber alert: Relative Humidity has spiked to 75 percent (Limit: 60 percent–65 percent). What is your mandatory standard operating procedure action?

PERFECT CRISIS CONTAINMENT! In the event of an environmental parameter breach, you must immediately halt pallet transit, seal airlock doors to isolate the chamber, and notify the Putaway Zone Leader and HVAC maintenance engineering. Never place sensitive cells into an out-of-spec vault!

CATASTROPHIC CONTAMINATION RISK! Never ignore an active environmental breach or attempt to bypass humidity trips. 75 percent RH triggers moisture condensation on lithium-ion terminals, creating hazardous internal micro-shorts and battery fires. Halt, isolate, and escalate immediately!

Final Stage 4 Battery Cell Challenge! Inside the battery standard room, floor space is tight. An operator notices two lithium-ion cell crates already stacked on a pallet position and attempts to hoist a third crate on top (3-high stacking) while also ignoring a triggered red ShockWatch indicator on the box corner. Should this be allowed or stopped immediately?
An operator attempts to stack battery cell crates 3-high on a storage pallet despite a triggered red ShockWatch impact indicator on the carton. Allow or halt?

STOP IS ABSOLUTELY MANDATORY! Lithium-ion battery cell crates have a strict maximum stacking limit of 2 crates high to prevent bottom pouch crushing and internal dielectric puncture. Furthermore, any red ShockWatch or tilt indicator trigger mandates immediate quarantine isolation and Quality Engineering review. Battery Cell Put-Away Module 4 is now 100 percent complete!

CRITICAL SAFETY HAZARD! Stacking 3 crates high crushes fragile lithium-ion pouches, risking electrolyte leakage and internal short-circuit fire. A red shock indicator means the shipment suffered severe impact during transit and cannot enter active assembly stock!

Welcome to Stage 5: Hazardous Chemicals & Thinners Put-Away! A supplier truck carrying drums of flammable thinners, paints, and hazardous solvents arrives at the Auric Main Gate. The driver asks if they should dock at Inbound Dock 01 (Main Assembly Building) with the other standard trucks. Under Ather where must chemical and thinner shipments proceed?
A delivery truck arrives with drums of combustible thinners and industrial paints. The driver asks to unload at Dock 01 next to vehicle body panels. Where does Ather mandate this vehicle proceed?

PERFECT FACILITY BYPASS ROUTING! Hazardous chemicals, thinners, and paints are stored in separate, designated buildings. The gate pass specifies the exact isolated building. Trucks must bypass the main assembly plant completely and dock directly at the detached Chemical Storage detached Chemical Annex, equipped with flameproof fixtures and spill berms!

CRITICAL INDUSTRIAL FIRE HAZARD! Hazardous solvents, combustible paints, and thinners must NEVER enter the main manufacturing plant or general Dock 01. Vapors or accidental leaks near high-voltage assembly lines create catastrophic explosion risks!

At Chemical Storage Annex, the truck has docked and an operator begins unloading 200-liter steel drums of industrial thinner. Take a close look at the unloading setup. Under Ather which critical safety hazard violates our mandatory chemical handling protocols?
Spot the Safety Violation: An operator is unloading 200L flammable thinner drums at Chemical Storage Annex. Which condition violates Ather safety protocols?

HAZARD SPOTTED! Flammable liquids must NEVER be staged on bare concrete without secondary spill containment, and steel drums must be clamped to an earthing reel before handling. Electrostatic discharge (ESD) can ignite volatile thinner fumes into an instant fireball, and uncontained spills create severe environmental contamination!

CRITICAL SAFETY RISK OVERLOOKED! Staging flammable solvent drums directly on bare concrete with disconnected grounding earthing wires is an extreme industrial hazard. A single static discharge spark can ignite the entire chemical warehouse!

Inside the Chemical Storage Annex, 4 different hazardous drums need to be slotted into storage. Chemical safety rules strictly prohibit storing incompatible classes in the same containment bay: mixing flammable solvents with oxidizers causes spontaneous explosion! In addition, Ather mandates all chemicals must be stowed within a strict 2-hour SLA. Sort each incoming drum into its compliant containment bay before time expires!
Segregate incoming chemicals into their designated storage bays according to Ather 2-Hour SLA limit.

CHEMICAL MATRIX COMPLIANCE ACHIEVED! Class 3 Flammables (Thinners & Paints), Class 5.1 Oxidizers (Peroxides), and Class 8 Corrosives (Pre-Treatment Acids) are fully segregated into isolated bund bays, and all stowing completed within the mandatory 2-hour SLA!

CRITICAL INCOMPATIBLE STORAGE HAZARD! Storing oxidizing agents next to flammable solvents causes exothermic decomposition and catastrophic chemical fires. Incompatible hazard classes must always be segregated into isolated sumps!

At Chemical Storage Annex, the put-away operator has successfully unloaded, inspected, and segregated 20 drums of industrial thinner into Bay 1. Who is responsible under Ather for generating the official Goods Receipt Note in SAP and posting the inventory stock into the ERP system?
After a chemical delivery truck is unloaded and physically verified at the Chemical Storage Annex, who is responsible for creating the Goods Receipt Note in SAP?

EXACT ROLE HANDOVER! The put-away operator conducts the physical unloading and verification check. Once verified, the Data Entry Operator generates the official Goods Receipt Note, affixes labels, and posts inventory into SAP warehouse management system when stowage is finished!

ROLE CONFUSION HAZARD! Put-away operators handle physical material movement, safety earthing, and stowage, but they do NOT generate the Goods Receipt Note. The Data Entry Operator is designated to generate the Goods Receipt Note and execute SAP inventory postings.

Urgent safety audit at Chemical Storage Annex! A drum of industrial thinner has been safely placed on the spill pallet. Before opening the bung cap to sample the viscosity, the operator reaches for the steel wrench without attaching the copper static earthing clamp to the plant grounding busbar. The operator insists, 'It's just a 10-second inspection.' Should this action be allowed or halted immediately?
An associate prepares to loosen a 200L solvent drum bung for QC sampling without attaching the static bonding grounding clamp. Allow or halt?

HALT IS THE ONLY SURVIVAL DECISION! Static electricity generated by wrench friction or liquid sloshing can spark an instantaneous vapor explosion exceeding 800 degrees Celsius! Grounding bonding clamps must be firmly connected to bare metal before touching or unsealing any flammable drum. Hazardous Chemicals & Thinners Module 5 is now 100 percent complete!

CATASTROPHIC FIRE VIOLATION! Flammable solvent vapors linger invisibly around drum bungs. Metal-on-metal spark without grounding causes immediate deflagration and factory-wide evacuation! Never loosen a chemical drum bung without active earthing!

Welcome to Stage 6: Supermarket C-Class Parts Put-Away! Small fasteners and grommets have arrived at the Material Handling staging desk from inbound receiving. The lot is marked Non-Direct-on-Line, but looking closely at the Goods Receipt Note sticker, the green 'QC Pass' circular stamp is completely missing! The line is waiting for these screws. Should the operator proceed to put these into the supermarket racks?

A Non-Direct-on-Line lot of small fasteners arrives at the supermarket receiving desk. The Goods Receipt Note sticker has no green 'QC Pass' seal attached. Allow or halt put-away into supermarket racks?

STOP IS THE CORRECT DECISION! standard operating procedure for Supermarket Put-Away For Non-Direct-on-Line parts, the physical 'QC Pass' seal or sticker is mandatory on the Goods Receipt Note label. Without this seal, the parts have NOT been released by Quality Control and could be defective. Moving uncertified parts to the supermarket risks line assembly defects and immediate vehicle recalls!

CRITICAL QUALITY BREACH! No associate may move a Non-Direct-on-Line lot to supermarket bins without a verified green 'QC Pass' seal. Rushing unverified parts to the line causes catastrophic vehicle assembly failures!

at the receiving desk, you print the SAP inventory dump from the system, which shows expected stock of 100 M6 hex bolts. You perform a sample count on the digital counting scale and find only 92 pieces—an 8-piece shortage! A line feeder says: 'Just put the 92 bolts into the bin so the line doesn't stop, and adjust the number later.' What is the mandatory standard operating procedure action under Ather?
The SAP stock report indicates 100 pieces for an inward C-class lot, but physical sampling at Material Handling reveals only 92 pieces. What must the operator do?

STANDARD PROCEDURE ENFORCED! If any discrepancy exists between the physical count and the SAP dump, the operator must IMMEDIATELY halt put-away for that material and escalate to the Supermarket Zone Leader. Never alter slips or stock short lots, as this creates ghost inventory that starves future production!

CRITICAL INVENTORY INTEGRITY FAILURE! Altering paperwork or stocking a short lot without Zone Leader escalation directly corrupts ERP stock accuracy. Downstream shifts will assume 100 bolts exist, resulting in sudden line starvation when only 92 are present!

Count audits are cleared! Now we proceed to the supermarket gravity flow racks. These 3.5-degree inclined roller tracks operate on strict First-In First-Out (First-In, First-Out). You must ALWAYS load from the REAR loading lane so boxes glide forward to the front picking face. Loading from the front traps older parts behind, causing reverse Last-In First-Out and part degradation. Arrange the 4 put-away steps in the exact standard operating procedure sequence!
Arrange the 4 steps of Supermarket Gravity Flow Rack Put-Away in the strictly mandated standard operating procedure sequence to guarantee First-In First-Out stock rotation.
Spot on! Your operational decision complies with Ather Auric standards.
Warning! protocol violation. Always follow standard operating procedure to maintain quality and safety.
Look at the front face of the supermarket rack! After assembly line kitters drew materials, the physical stock has reached the red MIN threshold (2 boxes remaining). What two.
The fastener bin has reached its safety minimum stock level of 2 boxes (200 pieces). What must the Supermarket operator execute immediately?
Spot on! Your operational decision complies with Ather Auric standards.
Warning! protocol violation. Always follow standard operating procedure to maintain quality and safety.

High tension at the supermarket receiving desk! You counted 92 bolts on the scale instead of 100. An aggressive line feeder arrives shouting that the main frame line is 2 minutes from stoppage! They demand: 'Sign off the full 100 pieces right now, hand me the bin, and let us fix the missing 8 pieces later in the week.' Do you allow this dispatch or stop immediately?
Physical count is 92 pcs (SAP expected: 100 pcs). Under urgent line-stoppage pressure, the line feeder demands you sign off 100 pcs immediately. Allow or Halt?

STOP IS ABSOLUTELY ESSENTIAL! Never sign a false count or release unverified quantities under line pressure! Discrepancy means an active halt for that material and instant escalation to the Supermarket Zone Leader. Falsifying records creates ghost inventory and leaves Ather legally exposed to supplier invoice fraud!

UNFORGIVABLE INVENTORY VIOLATION! Yielding to line pressure and falsifying 100 pieces when only 92 arrived destroys ERP audit trails. Next shift will run out of bolts midway, causing catastrophic unannounced line shutdown!
Final Supermarket certification question! Which parts are authorized to be stored in Supermarket flow racks at Ather Auric plant?
Which categories of parts are stored in Supermarket racks at the Ather Auric Plant?

PERFECT CLASSIFICATION MASTERY! Supermarket racks are designated EXCLUSIVELY for small C-class items (screws, bolts, clips, washers, O-rings) that are verified at the receiving desk first. Heavy A-class parts belong to High-Rise Racks and Trolley Staging! Stage 6: Supermarket C-Class Parts Put-Away is 100 percent complete!

INCORRECT CLASSIFICATION! Supermarket gravity racks cannot hold heavy A-class frames or flammable chemicals. Supermarket racks are strictly dedicated to small C-class hardware parts checked at the receiving desk!

Critical quality alert at quality inspection Test Bench 02! While inspecting a 10-piece sample from an incoming batch of 1,000 battery harness connectors, the inspector discovers 2 burnt, defective terminals with critical high resistance.
When quality inspection finds 2 defective burnt connectors in a 10-piece sample from a 1,000-piece lot, what materials must be moved to the NG Quarantine area?
Spot on! Your operational decision complies with Ather Auric standards.
Warning! protocol violation. Always follow standard operating procedure to maintain quality and safety.

The NG Logistics manpower team arrives at the quality inspection staging desk to collect a rejected pallet of high-voltage wiring harnesses. You inspect the pallet: it has a physical Red Tag affixed, but the QC sticker is missing, and the digital JIRA ticket has no Bug ID and lists root cause as 'Unknown'. For Rejected Return to Vendor what MUST the NG team do?
A rejected lot carries a Red Tag, but the QC sticker is missing and the JIRA ticket has no Bug ID ('Unknown Cause'). Can the NG team collect it?

ABSOLUTELY STOP! For Rejected Return to Vendor every rejected part MUST have BOTH a Red Tag AND a QC sticker, plus a JIRA ticket with a valid Bug ID! Collecting untracked parts creates ghost inventory and voids supplier warranty debit notes!
CRITICAL HAZARD! Never move rejected stock without dual physical identification (Red Tag + QC sticker) and an active JIRA Bug ID. Doing so causes untraceable inventory in the quarantine cage!

We have entered the high-security caged Quarantine Store! As rejected materials are stowed here, SAP moves inventory to Blocked Stock and the digital JIRA ticket transitions to 'Quality Failed'. How must rejected materials be segregated inside the cage?
Drag each rejected lot to its correct dedicated containment bay inside the Quarantine Cage based on its defect root cause.
Spot on! Your operational decision complies with Ather Auric standards.
Warning! protocol violation. Always follow standard operating procedure to maintain quality and safety.

The Material Review Board (Material Review Board) — comprising Supplier Quality Assurance, Manufacturing Quality, Production, and Warehouse — convenes inside caged store Quarantine Storage to decide the fate of 4 quarantined lots. Verbal approvals are strictly illegal at Ather Auric Plant M002! Route each quarantined component case study to its authorized disposition path (Auto-Return to Vendor, Rework, Use As-Is Deviation, or Scrap).
